title: Amazon Nears $7.5B Deal to Acquire AI Startup Decart
summary: Amazon is reportedly closing in on a $7.5 billion acquisition of AI startup Decart, marking one of the largest AI deals in 2026.
body_markdown:
#### 💡 TL;DR


- Amazon is reportedly finalizing a $7.5 billion acquisition of AI startup Decart in one of 2026's largest AI deals.
- The transaction would expand Amazon's AI capabilities and deepen its position in the competitive generative AI market.
- Financial terms remain under negotiation, with a formal announcement expected in the coming weeks or months.


Amazon is in advanced negotiations to acquire AI startup Decart for approximately $7.5 billion, according to reports from the Financial Times. The deal, if completed, would represent one of the largest AI-related acquisitions in 2026 and signal Amazon's accelerating push into artificial intelligence infrastructure and capabilities.


## Deal Structure and Financial Terms


Sources familiar with the matter indicate that Amazon and Decart are finalizing terms of the transaction, with the $7.5 billion valuation reflecting Decart's proprietary AI technology and market position. The acquisition is expected to be structured as a combination of cash and stock, though specific financial arrangements remain confidential as negotiations continue.


The deal would mark a significant premium over Decart's last known private valuation, underscoring the intense competition among major technology companies to secure cutting-edge AI assets. Industry analysts suggest the acquisition price reflects both Decart's existing technology portfolio and its team of specialized AI researchers and engineers.


## Decart's AI Technology and Market Position


Decart has built a reputation for developing specialized AI models focused on real-time processing and edge computing applications. The startup's technology stack includes proprietary algorithms for efficient neural network deployment and optimization tools that reduce computational overhead in production environments.


The company's client base spans multiple industries, including cloud services, autonomous systems, and enterprise software platforms. Decart's ability to deliver high-performance AI inference at scale has positioned it as an attractive target for companies seeking to enhance their AI infrastructure capabilities.


## Amazon's AI Strategy and Competitive Landscape


This acquisition aligns with Amazon's broader strategy to compete with Microsoft, Google, and other cloud providers in the artificial intelligence market. Amazon Web Services (AWS) has invested heavily in AI infrastructure, including custom silicon and machine learning services, but acquiring Decart would provide immediate access to proven technology and specialized talent.


The move comes as major technology companies escalate their AI investments through both internal development and strategic acquisitions. Earlier this year,[AMD closed its acquisition of World Labs](https://emergent.sh/news/amd-closes-world-labs-deal-8-2b-stock) for $8.2 billion, highlighting the aggressive M&A activity in the AI sector.


## Expected Release Timeline


The acquisition is rumored to release on an unspecified 2026 timeline, with sources suggesting a formal announcement could come within the next few weeks pending final regulatory and legal reviews. Amazon and Decart have declined to comment publicly on the transaction status.


Regulatory approval processes may extend the timeline, particularly given the deal's size and potential competitive implications. Antitrust authorities in multiple jurisdictions are expected to review the acquisition before it can close.


## What This Means


Amazon's pending acquisition of Decart represents a strategic bet on AI infrastructure and capabilities at a moment when generative AI and large-scale machine learning are reshaping enterprise technology. For Amazon, the deal offers immediate technical assets and human capital to accelerate its AI roadmap. For the broader market, it underscores the premium valuations and competitive intensity driving consolidation in the AI sector. If completed, this transaction will rank among the most significant AI acquisitions of 2026 and may set valuation benchmarks for future deals.
